articles.title: Plot targeting Manchester Jewish community disrupted, say police
articles.summary: Two men were arrested in Manchester on Sunday, say counter-terror police.
articles.body:
A "suspected terrorist plot" to target the Jewish community in Manchester is believed to have been foiled after two men were arrested in the city on Sunday, police have said.

The men, both in their 30s, were detained on suspicion of offences under Section 41 of the Terrorism Act 2000, according to the Metropolitan Police, which is leading the investigation.

Deputy Assistant Commissioner Vicki Evans said police were aware the news would cause "further concern" to the Jewish community "especially given the significant High Holy day period".

Yom Kippur - considered to be the holiest day in the Jewish calendar - was marked this year from Sunday evening to Monday evening.

The two suspects remain in police custody after being taken to a London police station for questioning.

Police said the investigation related to a "suspected terrorist plot to target the Jewish community in the Manchester area".

"This has been a long-running proactive investigation which has led to the disruption of what we believe to be a plot to target the Jewish community in the Manchester area," said Evans.

"Counter-terrorism policing (CTP) continue to focus our efforts on identifying and disrupting those who wish to cause harm in our communities.

"Importantly, we do not believe there to be any ongoing threat to the public in relation to this matter, but as ever, we would ask that people remain vigilant and contact police with any concerns."

The two suspects were arrested on Newton Street in the Northern Quarter area of Manchester at 14:45 BST.

Detectives have obtained warrants of further detention for both men, meaning they can remain in police custody until 27 September.

Police confirmed searches at properties on Epworth Street in Liverpool and Lancaster Road in Salford had now been completed.

Evans, who is the senior national co-ordinator for CTP, said: "We are acutely aware this news will cause further concern to the Jewish community, as well as the wider public, especially given the significant High Holy day period.

"I want to reassure them we are working incredibly closely with colleagues in Greater Manchester Police and partners to ensure we're doing everything we can to keep them and the wider public safe.

"And more broadly across the country, CTP is working with local police forces to provide protective security support and advice for areas with Jewish communities, and particularly during the High Holy Day period."

A spokesperson for the Community Security Trust, which coordinates security for Jewish communities in the UK, said the suspected plot was "utterly chilling coming so close to the anniversary of the terrorist attack at Heaton Park Synagogue last year".

They added: "[This] is another reminder of the serious terrorist threat facing Jewish communities in this current time."

articles.title: 50 travel destinations to inspire you for 2027, chosen by Lonely Planet
articles.summary: There’s a new travel season just around the corner and Lonely Planet has released its list of 50 destinations and experiences to inspire your adventures in the year ahead.
articles.body: Don’t put your bikini in storage just yet. There’s a new travel season just around the corner and Lonely Planet has released its list of 50 destinations and experiences to inspire your adventures in the year ahead. The 53-year-old guidebook company launched the Lonely Planet app earlier this year, so explorers can for the first time adopt a triple-threat approach to their trip planning, using the app, the Lonely Planet booking platform Journeys, and the best-selling books. “We are about to hit 100,000 downloads in five months,” says Nitya Chambers, Lonely Planet’s senior vice president of content and executive editor. “And we’ve created some app-exclusive destination content for Best in Travel.” The Best in Travel 2027 list, available online and as a commemorative book, was selected by Lonely Planet’s global community of travel experts, and covers everything from longboat trips to orangutan territory in Malaysia to an early Christian pilgrimage route to Lindisfarne in northeast England. “I think what’s exciting to us is that there’s not just one kind of trip we’re telling people to take. It’s really about finding the experience that speaks to what someone wants from travel right now,” says Chambers, “You know, diving in the Aegean Sea, eating your way through Taiwan” or “eating crabs in Maryland” and “kayaking through Okinawa.” ‘Awe-inspiring and otherworldly’ California’s Coastal Redwoods are one of Chambers’ favorites on the 2027 list. They’re “the tallest trees on Earth. They’re centuries old,” she says. “I think there’s something about standing among them that makes you feel really small in the best possible way, and you’re just still inside of something so magnificent.” A different kind of immersive experience is offered in Newport, Rhode Island, where visitors can volunteer as overnight or weekly guest lighthouse keepers, taking on chores and general maintenance. European city picks include Dessau, Germany — home of the revolutionary Bauhaus architecture and design movement — and historic Verona and Padua in Italy’s underrated Veneto region. “The list is really meant to be a range of experiences that feel really accessible and actionable, and you could fit into a weekend, and things that are awe-inspiring and otherworldly,” says Chambers. A polar plunge in Antarctica is “a giant bucket list one,” she says. “I think anytime someone goes to Antarctica and comes back, they are like cloaked in awe. Like they have an awe filter on them, and that is how they are engaging with the world.” Push yourself to new challenges Monteverde’s cloud forest in Costa Rica is another perspective-changing experience. “You’re standing above the world in something that feels so ancient and so alive,” says Chambers, “and it’s such a different vantage from which to view” our planet. Wildlife experiences include a safari trek in Tanzania’s Gombe National Park, made famous by the late Jane Goodall, who began her pioneering work with chimpanzees here in 1960. Kenya’s Tsavo East and West National Parks are also among the 2027 picks. Pacific island adventures await in New Caledonia, famous for its UNESCO-recognized lagoons, and Samoa, whose traditional culture known as Faʻa Sāmoa is one of the experiential recommendations for 2027. The Chinese city of Chengdu is renowned for its Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding, but is also a celebrated gastronomical center, and in Kazakhstan, the spectacular architecture of capital Astana gets a shout-out. “You want to come home slightly changed,” says Chambers. “You want to push yourself to do something that you might not have considered doing, and then you come back a new person.” Lonely Planet’s Best in Travel 2027 North America Places Experiences Europe Places Experiences Caribbean, Central America, South America Places Experiences Africa & Middle East Places Experiences Oceania Places Experiences Asia Places Experiences

articles.title: From tariff overlord to tarmac man, Donald Trump to roll out red carpet for Xi Jinping
articles.summary: US News: TOI correspondent from Washington: Donald Trump has spent years telling Americans that China has been eating America's lunch. On Wednesday, he will go.
articles.body: TOI correspondent from Washington: Donald Trump has spent years telling Americans that China has been eating America's lunch. On Wednesday, he will go to the airport to welcome the man who owns the restaurant.In an unprecedented spectacle, Trump will schlep where no US President has gone before – travel to Andrews Air Force Base outside Washington, DC, to personally receive Chinese President Xi Jinping as he arrives for a three-day state visit, briefly transforming himself from an imperious tariff overlord to a deferential tarmac man.The optics will be hard to miss. Xi's airbase reception is to be followed by an elaborate ceremonial welcome at the White House the following day, including a 479-member military honour guard, a presidential salute and military review in the Rose Garden, and a flyover featuring a B-2 Spirit bomber escorted by four F-22 Raptors in a show aimed at impressing a country that appears to have passed the stage of being impressed.Diplomatic scholars are already weighing in, noting that the last US Presidents to go to the airport to receive a foreign dignitary were Obama and Bush, who went to Andrews AFB to receive Pope Francis and Pope Benedict, respectively.Xi did not go to the airport to welcome the US President when Trump went on a state visit in May and instead sent his Vice President Han Zheng and other officials.“Xi wasn't waiting for him, there were no flyovers, and there was no meeting of the first ladies…the asymmetry in pageantry reflects a broader asymmetry in the relationship: Beijing believes rare earths tamed Washington, and Washington at times seems to agree,” noted Rush Doshi, a former NSC official whose remit in the Biden administration included China and Taiwan.Trump has spent years portraying China as the villain in America's economic travails -- stealer of American jobs, manipulator of trade, technological predator and beneficiary of what he has repeatedly described as an unfair trading relationship. He launched a tariff war designed to force Beijing to bend, but Doshi sees China emerging as a peer instead.“Beijing’s ability to turn back US tariffs marked an inflexion point that established China as a true peer of the US, albeit one ahead on some metrics of power and behind on others,” he wrote in a preview of the summit.Having flexed its rare earths muscle, China doesn’t seem too impressed either by Trump rolling out US corporate power -- or American oligarchy in the eyes of some critics.Jeff Bezos, Elon Musk, Jensen Huang, Sam Altman, Tim Cook, Jane Fraser, and Michael Dell are among those slated to attend a Trump-Xi meeting, a powerlist topped by two Indian-Americans – Google’s Sundar Pichai and Microsoft's Satya Nadella.Xi conspicuously is not bringing any notable Chinese executives with him.Trade and tariffs are expected to dominate the agenda, with an extension of the fragile trade truce, possible reciprocal tariff reductions, agricultural purchases and mechanisms for managing bilateral commerce up for discussion.The leaders are also expected to discuss rare earths and critical minerals, semiconductor export controls, artificial intelligence, intellectual property and technology restrictions.Then there are the geopolitical files – Taiwan, Iran, the Strait of Hormuz and Ukraine – where the two sides are locked in indirect conflict. While neither side is calling it a G-2, it is increasingly starting to look like that, to much consternation in India, which has benefited from American efforts to diversify supply chains away from China.While a prolonged technology confrontation has encouraged manufacturers to consider India as an alternative production base, a US-Chinese accommodation could reduce some of that strategic pressure on Beijing.At the same time, Indian mandarins say New Delhi has no interest in seeing Washington and Beijing stumble into confrontation over Taiwan, rare earths or the South China Sea. Nor does it want the global economy repeatedly held hostage by tariff exchanges between its two largest external economic partners.The Indian calculation, therefore, is less about choosing Washington over Beijing than ensuring that an emerging G2 does not become a condominium over Asia.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.body:
President Trump on Tuesday signed a trilateral security agreement with Greenland and Denmark on the sidelines of the U.N. General Assembly in New York City.

“We’re going to have a tremendous relationship, a secure relationship, and we look forward to it,” Trump said during the signing ceremony. “We’ll be working very hard and very much in conjunction with each other.”

The deal, which the president first announced earlier this month , includes establishing two new U.S. military bases on the arctic island. The move comes after months of scrutiny over the Trump administration’s threat to take over Greenland.

articles.title: South Korean president says Trump should ease sanctions on North Korea
articles.summary: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung broke from precedent by urging President Trump to ease sanctions on North Korea in an exchange that would put a halt on its weapons programs. Lee told The New York Times in a Friday interview that he sees “significant value” in trading between sanctions and freezing North Korea’s development…
articles.body:
South Korean President Lee Jae Myung broke from precedent by urging President Trump to ease sanctions on North Korea in an exchange that would put a halt on its weapons programs.

Lee told The New York Times in a Friday interview that he sees “significant value” in trading between sanctions and freezing North Korea’s development of nuclear weapons.

“Aiming for denuclearization under the current circumstances guarantees that nothing will be accomplished,” Lee warned, insisting to the Times that diplomacy is the last option left in handling North Korea.

He told the outlet the freeze on developing weapons will result from concessions and reciprocal incentives, ultimately leaving North Korean leader Kim Jong Un and other officials with a sense of security that does not rely on nuclear weapons.

Lee expressed hope that the U.S. and North Korea opening a dialogue will help his country’s relations with its neighbor to the north, as Pyongyang strengthens its relations with Russia and China, the Times reported. North Korea has opened one bridge with Russia, while another with China is close to opening.

The South Korean president told the outlet that the stalemate is a risk as North Korea builds up its nuclear stockpile.

“Our estimates suggest that North Korea is now capable of producing, or may already be producing, an additional 10 to 20 nuclear weapons each year,” Lee said. “Once it believes it has accumulated enough nuclear weapons and missiles to guarantee its survival, it will be tempted to export them to make money.”

He added that “will be a truly dangerous moment.”

Lee also told The Associated Press that North Korea has refused to hold any dialogue as it ramps up its missile tests. Lee called for a “phased approach of stopping, reduction and dismantlement” of North Korea’s weapons supply, saying he would advance this plan at the United Nations General Assembly in New York this week.

Lee’s government is also looking to alleviate trade tensions with the U.S., with negotiators working to implement a $350 billion deal to lower tariffs agreed to with Trump in October. The Times noted that South Korea could offer to build a gas power plant in Texas and eight nuclear power plants across the U.S. to appease Trump, according to people familiar with the matter.

Trump said last year that South Korea agreed to purchase U.S. oil and gas in “vast quantities” and declared that their countries’ military alliance was “stronger than ever before.”

Trump and Kim first met in 2018, which led to the development of what Trump would frequently call a friendship with the dictator. The two exchanged letters with one another, with Trump referring to his letter from Kim in August 2019 as “beautiful.”

The U.S. president claimed in August that he would meet with Kim in 2026 and that he gets “along with him very well.” However, Kim’s younger sister, Kim Yo Jong, said at the time that North Korea’s position on the U.S. has not changed and cast doubt on a future meeting, The Guardian reported.
